# Additive tuning of 2026-11-02, engine round 1 best so far, scenario 2

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
tree: sha256:e20328782b6ec97c1eb3888c40655c821ff9bf42074e3f8dca179b838644d038
lock: sha256:826dcf9f83c5d9e7fb557d7a1df9753a09a5c70c645d6c9faf7a575256119178
selection: sha256:d99530b2b639bb6bdd279be2a9356a64ce2a0c8cceca354d56957f198a76a20a
read_set: sha256:2a47d5b0401ca6d3239d352781fe101f4d7ba74c60c6a0dbe460e46ae9703c4d
seed: 0
harness: 0.6.1
tier: additive
arm: scenario-2
at: 2026-11-02
cost_cents: 12631
```

**This line is the `best` stage of round 1 of the engine layer, measured again, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1877](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877) asked for.** It replaces [the first measurement of the best so far](additive-tuning-of-2026-10-31-engine-round-1-best-so-far-scenario-2.md), which passed 67 of 144. The owner voided that measurement [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6568926331), because its oracles graded a tree that missed the files a session deleted or moved through the shell. [#1923](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1923) fixed the grading tree, and this line measures scenario 2, the documents and the engine as they stand, again with the fixed grader. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-2 tuning`. It is the `scenario-2` arm of the additive tier over the 22 probes of the tuning set, at 7 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288.

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `329f3362` for the whole batch. That commit differs from the base pin `b85f1704` only by [#1926](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/pull/1926), which recorded the base and changed no source of the engine. The canary of 8 sessions held 4 records that named paths outside the workspace: each searched outside its workspace in the same pattern as the canaries before it, and the sandbox binds none of those paths. The owner read them and [passed the canary](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1877#issuecomment-6577995874). The driver then halted 11 times on a harness failure of the kind that a usage limit causes. The last halt returned the plan's session limit, and the driver continued in the same try root at the same pin after its reset. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 154 sessions and cost 12631 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 1 stopped at the turn cap, 0 stopped at the session budget, 115 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. 53 of the 154 sessions called the engine. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 2 passed 112 of the 154 sessions it graded, 73%. The voided measurement passed 67 of 144, 47%, over the same 22 probes. The base row compares this measurement with the base of scenario 1 at `b85f1704`, which passed 81 of 154 in [the base transcript](additive-tuning-of-2026-11-02-base-re-measure-of-scenario-1.md). The difference is +20.1 points, with the interval [+9.3, +30.3]. The interval does not include zero. The keep rule reads only a confirmation, and a best so far is never kept. This line is the number that each screened rewording of the engine layer is compared with, and the engine layer ranks by pass rate.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 15000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 13696 cents against its cap, and the 154 recorded sessions account for 12631 cents of that sum. The difference is the sessions that recorded nothing because the harness halted them. `try.sh spent` counts the 13696 cents against the ceiling of 103300 cents for the tries, which now stands at 27811 cents.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1877/engine-r1-best-2/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.

    - tool: "SendMessage"
      argument: "{\"to\":\"main\",\"summary\":\"Early answer: hashing mechanism + bless command, before full report\",\"message\":\"Quick answer so you're unblocked; full categorized report follows shortly.\\n\\nHASHING: `verified_revision` is NOT a plain sha256 of file content. Chain is:\\n1. `engine/crates/hash/src/lib.rs::digest(bytes) -> \\\"sha256:<hex>\\\"` — plain sha256 of whatever bytes it's given.\\n2. `engine/crates/graph/src/anchors.rs::tree_revision(base, matched) / tree_revision_in` — for EVERY regular file in the anchor's `matched` list (sorted+deduped), it reads the file's raw bytes (`std::fs::read`) and computes `digest(bytes)` per file via `FileDigests::of`. It then builds a manifest string of lines `\\\"{path}\\\\0{per_file_digest}\\\\n\\\"` for each matched file (sorted by path), and returns `digest(manifest.as_bytes())`.\\n   => So even a SINGLE-file `governs`/`traces_to` target (e.g. `engine/crates/check/src/language.rs`) is NOT `sha256(file_bytes)` directly — it's `sha256(\\\"<path>\\\\0sha256:<hex of file bytes>\\\\n\\\")`. A glob like `tools/engine/harper-spike/**` hashes one manifest line per matched file, so editing ANY file under that glob changes the digest.\\n3. Stored/compared via `headwater_graph::edges::VERIFIED_REVISION` const (`\\\"verified_revision\\\"`) and `Edge::verified_revision()`/`Edge::suspect_revisions()` in `engine/crates/graph/src/edges.rs` (lines ~121, 379-402). The \\\"current\\\" value compared against is `Target::Anchor.revision` = `tree_revision` evaluated fresh against the working tree (not git, no VCS call).\\n\\nPRACTICAL IMPACT FOR YOUR EDITS:\\n- `docs/evaluations/harper-spike-results.md` governs `tools/engine/harper-spike/**` WITH `verified_revision: sha256:432b2bb6...`. Editing ANY file under `tools/engine/harper-spike/` will change this digest and make that edge \\\"suspect\\\" (flagged by the `relation.target.suspect` check-layer rule in `engine/crates/check/src/suspect.rs`).\\n- `engine/crates/check/src/language.rs`: decision 0087 cites it `- to: engine/crates/check/src/language.rs` WITH `verified_revision: sha256:73b6425e...` — editing that file WILL make 0087's edge suspect. Decision 0069 cites the same file as a bare string (`governs: - engine/crates/check/src/language.rs`, no `verified_revision`) — that edge can NEVER go suspect (no revision recorded), only the path string matters for it. `docs/evaluations/what-a-check-can-know.md` cites it under `traces_to` also as a bare string — same, no revision, path-only.\\n\\nBLESS/RECOMPUTE: There is NO automated \\\"bless\\\" command that rewrites `verified_revision` or `last_verified` in doc frontmatter (unlike `HEADWATER_BLESS=1 cargo test` which only re-records *test fixtures*, e.g. `engine/crates/graph/fixtures/corpus.graph` — that's a different, unrelated mechanism for engine-internal test snapshots, not for doc frontmatter). The real mechanism is the CLI itself:\\n- `headwater check --fix --change` is the command that recomputes and writes `verified_revision` onto a suspect edge (see `engine/crates/check/src/suspect.rs` doc comments ~line 113-160, and `engine/crates/cli/src/lib.rs` ~line 494/506). It only offers the patch when the run's `--change` input states a person actually re-verified the edge (the declaring doc's freshness facet moved, e.g. `last_verified`, or a `verified\\\\t<doc>\\\\t<target>` line) — it deliberately will NOT silently \\\"re-stamp\\\" an edge nobody re-read. So after you edit files, you'll need to run `headwater check --fix --change <changefile>` (or add a `verified` line / bump `last_verified` appropriately) rather than expect an automatic recompute.\\n\\nFull report with the `relation.target.unresolved` existence-check test and the complete categorized \\\"language.rs\\\" grep list coming next.\",\"type\":\"message\",\"recipient\":\"main\",\"content\":\"Quick answer so you're unblocked; full categorize…\"}"
